title: Position Sizing
hook: Risk only what you can afford to lose. Size your position, not your ego.

launchpad.outcome: Explain why the same setup can be smart at one size and reckless at another.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If two traders take the identical setup but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10, is one trade objectively better structured?

markers.label: Size your position, not your ego

slides.headline: Size your position, not your ego.
slides.line: Your entry can be clean and your stop correct. Too much size still makes the trade heavy.

slides.kicker: Contracts change the money, not the structure
slides.headline: The chart doesn’t know your size. You do.
slides.line: Position sizing is what makes the same setup feel manageable or reckless.

tool.title: Tap each size to see how the weight changes
tool.body: Same 10-point stop, same setup, only the contract count changes below.

slides.headline: After a loss, you double your size.
slides.line: You want to “win it back faster.”

visual.caption: Bigger size, right after a loss.

options.label: A smart way to recover losses quickly
options.feedback: Increasing size to chase back a loss usually increases risk at the worst possible moment.

options.label: Emotion is driving your size, not your risk plan
options.why: Exactly. That’s revenge sizing, and it compounds risk right when discipline matters most.

slides.headline: 1 contract or 10. Same setup.
slides.line: Same entry, same stop, same target.

check.prompt: Is one trade objectively better structured?

options.label: Yes, more contracts is a better trade
options.feedback: More contracts just means more exposure. It doesn’t improve the setup itself.

options.label: Yes, fewer contracts is a more valid setup
options.feedback: Fewer contracts reduces dollar risk, but it doesn’t change whether the setup itself was valid.

options.label: No, only the dollar risk and weight differ
options.why: The structure is identical. Sizing decides how much is on the line, it doesn’t change whether the setup itself is good.

slides.headline: Same rule. Same size.
slides.line: Decide your contract size the same way every time, not by how you feel that day.

check.prompt: Your contract size should be decided by your ___, not by how confident you feel today.

options.label: Mood
options.feedback: Mood changes day to day. Your sizing shouldn’t.

options.label: Risk plan
options.why: A risk plan stays consistent regardless of how a trader feels in the moment.

options.label: Win streak
options.feedback: A win streak doesn’t change how much risk a setup can actually handle.

slides.line: Going heavier because confidence is high, or doubling size after a loss, is emotion talking, not a risk plan.

slides.prompt: Why isn’t bigger size just a faster way to make money?
slides.modelAnswer: Bigger size doesn’t make a bad setup good, and it doesn’t make a good setup better, it just multiplies whatever is already there, including the emotional weight of being wrong. The same setup that’s easy to think clearly through at 1 contract can become impossible to manage at 10, even though nothing about the chart changed.

takeaways: Position size decides how much dollar risk and emotional weight a trade carries.
The same setup can be reasonable at a small size and reckless at an oversized one.
Sizing should come from your risk plan, never from mood or a win/loss streak.
remember: Size your position, not your ego.
